name: Boolean simplification
description: Flags a Bool compared with == or != against true or false, since the value or its negation already says the same thing. The fix rewrites it to the value or '! value'.
definition: Flags, as an `[info]`, a `==` or `!=` comparison between a `Bool` value and a `true`/`false` literal (in either order), including `!=`. `flag == true` and `flag != false` are the same as `flag`; `flag == false` and `flag != true` are the same as `! flag`. Only an operand whose type is known to be `Bool` is rewritten: a local, parameter, property, script variable, literal, cast, comparison, or logical expression. A call, member access, or any other operand whose type can't be determined locally is left alone, and so is a non-`Bool` operand (an `Int` compared with `true` belongs to the strict-boolean and type rules, not this one). A comparison inside a full property's Get/Set block is not checked, because those blocks are not part of the parsed AST. Automatically fixable: the fix replaces the comparison with the value or with `! value` (one space after `!`, parentheses when the negated expression needs them) and folds a comparison of two boolean literals down to `true` or `false`.
